जब वे छाता तथा चामर जेसी साज-सामग्र सहित अपने संगियों के साथ आगे आये तो श्चेत

Sanak and other sages saw that Lord Vishnu, who in his emotional meditation, was previously visible only within their hearts,
Now he is appearing in a tangible form before their eyes.
When they came forward with their companions, including umbrellas and brooms, with all their equipment, then the hairs of the broom were slowly moving, as if there were two white swans, and with the favorable wind, the pearl garlands hanging from the umbrella
were also moving, as if drops of nectar were dripping from a full moon, or as if the snow was melting from a gust of wind. Meaning: In this verse, the word 'achakshatakshavishayam' has come. God does not appear to the ordinary people,
But now he was becoming visible to the eyes of TUR. Another important word is Samadhi Bhagam. Those
meditators who are very fortunate, they can see the form of Lord Vishnu within their hearts through the method of yoga. But seeing them in person is a different matter. This is only possible for pure devotees.
It is possible. Therefore, when Kumaras saw that God was coming with his companions, who were carrying umbrellas and
whisks, they were astonished that they were directly seeing God.
Brahma-
It is said in the Samhita that the devotees who are always in love with God, within their limits, always see Lord
Shyamasundar. But when they mature, then the same God appears directly before them. Ordinary people do not see God, but when someone can understand the importance of God's holy name,
and by starting with the tongue through chanting and the taste of Prasad, and by engaging oneself in devotion to God,
God himself appears in it gradually. In this way, the devotee constantly sees God in his heart, and in a more mature state, he directly sees that same God

God is the abode of all bliss. His auspicious presence is for the blessings of everyone.
And his loving smile and gaze touch the innermost of the heart. The beautiful
color of God's body is dark, and his broad chest is the resting place of Lakshmiji, which is the entire
the divine that glorifies the entire spiritual world, which is the pinnacle of all
heavenly realms. In this way,
It seemed as if God himself was expanding the beauty and good fortune of the spiritual world.
He was expanding. Meaning: When the Lord came, he was pleased with everyone; that is why it is said here that Kritsn
Prasad-yumrukham. God knew that even the guilty gatekeeper was his pure devotee, although coincidentally he
committed an offense at the feet of other devotees. In devotion, committing an offense against a devotee is extremely fatal.
It happens. That is why Shri Chaitanya Mahaprabhu has said that the offense committed against a devotee is like that intoxicated elephant
that runs here and there.
When a mad elephant enters a garden, it crushes all the plants. Similarly, the offense committed at the feet of a pure devotee destroys his position in devotion.
As far as God is concerned, he was not in any humiliating posture, because he does not accept any offense committed by his
devout devotee. But a devotee should be very careful about committing offenses against the feet of another devotee. To have equanimity on all and to be especially inclined towards his devotees, the Lord looked upon those who committed offenses with the same compassion as those who were to be offended.
As much as those who were to be offended. This is the nature of God, being an infinite treasure of divine qualities

485. Their pleasant demeanor towards the devotees was so captivating and heart-touching that even their smile
became attractive to them. That attraction was not only divine for all the higher realms of this physical world,
but also for the spiritual world beyond it. Generally, people cannot guess what the natural state is in those higher realms, who, from the point of view of all the equipment,
are extremely prosperous, yet Vaikuntha Loka is so pleasant and so divine that its analogy
is given by a gem in the middle of a garland of gems or a locket. In this verse, the word 'Sprhanya-Dham' indicates that God is the abode of all bliss,
because all divine qualities are found in Him. Although those who are eager for the bliss of being one with the formless Brahman,
they desire only a few of these qualities, but there are also some
who are desirous, who want to have direct association with God as His servants.
God is so merciful
that he gives refuge to everyone, whether they are non-discriminatory or devotees. They give refuge to the Nirvisheshvadis in their
